name: Takht-e Soleyman
description: Takht-e Soleyman is a ruined fortified complex in north-western Iran, near the town of Takab, built on a mound formed by a calcium-rich spring and its small lake. It was home to Adur Gushnasp, a Sasanian fire temple where kings once humbled themselves before a sacred flame. Later Mongol rebuilding and local legends of King Solomon imprisoning monsters in a nearby crater add layers of story.
